title: Blaschka auction provenance cross-links and market-adjacent leads
purpose: Supplement the canonical auction lot table with cross-source identity hypotheses, prior institutional labels, dealer-market leads, and bounded negative-search results that should not be flattened into auction facts without an explicit evidential bridge.

relationship_to_canonical.rule: This file records evidence that qualifies or extends canonical auction records without silently upgrading inferred buyer identities, dealer transactions, institutional labels, or conflicting dates into settled provenance.

evidence: Invaluable indexes a Grisebach sale on 26 November 2015 for a Blaschka Serpulidae model labelled Serpula contortuplicata, L. No. 343, with dimensions approximately 6 cm high by 9.5 cm diameter and estimate EUR 3,000-5,000.
Grisebach's own 2015 press material identifies ORANGERIE. Selected Objects as the relevant 26 November 2015 crossover object sale in Berlin.

In a first-person Corning Museum of Glass guest post, George Loudon states that he had recently found a Blaschka model of a Serpulidae worm at auction in Berlin; the illustrated object is identified as Serpula contortuplicata and measured 6 x 9 cm diameter, with a 2015 Berlin photograph credit.
Taxon, object type, city, time, dimensions and 2015 documentation align very closely, but Loudon's account does not name Grisebach, a lot number or L. No. 343.
crosslinks.safe_public_claim: George Loudon's 2016 first-person account appears to describe the same Serpula contortuplicata model sold through Grisebach in Berlin in November 2015, but the buyer identity remains an inference until a buyer record, invoice, catalogue annotation, or explicit collection crosswalk is recovered.
open_fields: explicit buyer record or invoice linking the lot to George Loudon

crosslinks.prior_institutional_label: Zoolog. Institut Universität, Berlin / handwritten botanical designation
crosslinks.institutional_interpretation: The wording is consistent with a Berlin university zoological-institute teaching-collection label. It establishes a prior Berlin institutional association at label level, not an original-purchase, legal-title, deaccession, or current-institution identity by itself.

date_conflict.Berlin_institutional_collection_context: Museum für Naturkunde Berlin states that all Berlin Blaschka models in its historical university/museum collection were made between 1884 and 1889.
date_conflict.guard: Do not normalize the auction-house circa-1870 date to 1884-1889 and do not assume that the label necessarily places the object in the surviving MfN/HU corpus without an inventory crosswalk.

market_adjacent_leads.reported_context: Loudon states that a London dealer obtained the Blaschka pieces from an English school that had closed or was disposing of its natural-history teaching material for financial reasons. These purchases helped form the Blaschka component of his collection before the 2015 Berlin auction acquisition.
market_adjacent_leads.why_not_auction_record: The source describes purchases through a dealer, not a public auction event. It is therefore retained as a provenance-gap lead but excluded from auction lot totals.
open_fields: model catalogue numbers and current object crosswalk

institutional_context_only.statement: UCL Grant Museum states that when the Science Museum deaccessioned its glass-model collection in 1925-1927, models were transferred to UCL and six other institutions. This establishes a wider deaccession/distribution event but does not identify the later Christie's objects as part of those institutional transfers.
institutional_context_only.guard: Do not infer an intermediate institutional owner for the three 2019 Christie's lots without matching Science Museum transfer records or recipient accession numbers.

bounded_negative_search.result: No additional vetted physical Blaschka auction lot was promoted in this continuation pass.
areas_rechecked: English, German, French and Italian keyword variants

bounded_negative_search.important_negative_guard: Search-engine and public-index failure is not catalogue exhaustion. Older PDF, print-only, poorly OCRed, subscriber-only and unindexed sale catalogues remain outside the closure claim.
